newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Some flights on, Cambodia evacuation continues.
newsitem.headline: Some flights on, Cambodia evacuation continues.

text.p: International commercial flights resumed from Phnom Penh's airport on Wednesday, four days after fighting in the capital closed the facility and left the newly renovated terminal in ruins.
However, Cambodia's Southeast Asian neighbours were still evacuating their nationals on special flights from the capital.
"We have three flights on Vietnam Airlines to Saigon (Ho Chi Minh City) and two flights to Saigon on Royal Air Cambodge," said Keo Sophal, secretary general of the civil aviation authority.

Limited domestic flights also resumed on Wednesday, with four flights between Phnom Penh and the northern tourist city of Siem Reap, he said. No flights had yet resumed to Cambodia's second city of Battambang, he added.
Flights to Bangkok by Cambodia's flag carrier, Royal Air Cambodge, were due to resume on Thursday, another aviation official said.
"Everything is step by step back to normal," Keo Sivorn, director of operations for the aviation authority, told Reuters. "Tomorrow, we have two Air Cambodge flights to Bangkok."
Civil aviation authority representatives were meeting officials from Malaysian Airlines to discuss the possibility of resuming services to Kuala Lumpur, Keo Sophal said.

The first flights to arrive in Cambodia since a weekend of fighting and a subsequent day of looting were Thai air force planes, which made repeated trips on Tuesday, evacuating nearly 800 people, most of them Thai.
Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines all sent special aircraft into Phnom Penh on Wednesday to evacuate hundreds of their citizens.
The foreigners, eager to leave the quiet but still very tense city, received boarding cards and immigration forms in the open air, next to the gutted and blasted-out terminal building.
Japan sent three military aircraft to its southernmost air base of Okinawa on Wednesday to stand by for a possible evacuation of its citizens from the country.
